title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 3 vs. San Francisco 49ers
headline: Coach praised Jeremiyah Love for handling a bigger workload but would not commit to how it will look going forward.
summary: LaFleur said there was nothing to report on injuries, since no player left the game with more than a minor bump. He explained the late decision to kick a field goal instead of waiting for a touchdown: it cut the deficit to one score and let the team still try an onside kick and run normal plays. On defense he said the group needs to get to the quarterback more consistently, keep rush lanes disciplined, and tackle better, while crediting the opposing quarterback's ability to escape pressure. He said the team was moving the ball and running effectively but lacked explosive plays, and that penalties were the main reason they lost ground, especially in the second half. He praised the offensive line's effort but said pass protection on play-action got leaky for Jacoby Brissett, which the staff will review. On Jeremiyah Love, he said Love found a rhythm, stayed disciplined with his reads, and handled the heavier load well, while declining to say whether that role will continue. On the defensive side, he said the heavy base and two-tight-end looks were meant to take air out of the coverages used by similar offenses, and that the plan will change for next week's different opponent.

signals.claim: Handled an increased workload well; future workload will be decided week to week
signals.note: A bigger role was validated by the coach, but he hedged on whether the increased usage continues, so monitor next week's touch counts.
signals.quote: I thought he handled the workload well.

signals.claim: Has done a really good job in the defensive backer role and will keep playing there
signals.note: Praise for his play suggests he remains a fixed starter in the linebacker group, which supports his tackle volume.
signals.quote: Gibby's done a really good job.

signals.claim: Coaches have a lot of trust in him and he is part of the backer group
signals.note: Stated trust suggests a stable role alongside Gibbens, though the coach did not give a specific snap or role change.
signals.quote: We have a lot of trust in Cody Simon too.

topics.detail: LaFleur said penalties were the main reason the offense lost ground, and the team played cleaner and scored more once they were reduced in the second half.
The rushing attack was efficient and often created second-and-manageable situations, but the longest run was only eight yards, and the coach said the team has not yet hit a big play.

The defense played heavy base personnel with a fullback and at least two tight ends against similar offenses. LaFleur said the plan will change for next week's opponent and that the blitz approach may not look the same.
The defense needs to get more pressure on the quarterback and be disciplined in rush lanes, because the opposing quarterback escapes well.
The line battled in all phases, but pass protection on play-action shots was leaky at times, and the staff will review how long linemen are asked to hold up.

title: Joe Brady Talks What He Learned From the 24-16 Victory Over the Chargers
headline: Bills won ugly (24-16) despite five turnovers; Ty Johnson made big plays and James Cook keeps the job despite a second straight fumble, while Christian Benford's injury status is unknown.
summary: Joe Brady took the blame for five offensive turnovers in the 24-16 win over the Chargers. He called the day a fire alarm after weeks of talking about "smoke detectors" on ball security. He praised the defense for keeping the team in the game and highlighted C.J. Gardner-Johnson's interception in his return. He said he told the team at halftime the situation was "perfect" as a test of character. Brady said Greg Rousseau is playing a slightly different position with eyes in the backfield and a two-point stance, and that his confidence could open things up for Ed Oliver, Dion Dawkins and Bradley Chubb. Ty Johnson brought energy and playmaking, with a designed fourth-down play and a big third-down conversion, and it was good to get Frank Gore Jr. back involved. Brady stood by James Cook after a second straight game with a punched-out ball, saying he told Cook he would still get the ball on the next play. On injuries, he had no update on Christian Benford, who went down, and Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun filled in. He said he will review the pass protection issues, starting with his own play calling, and defended Josh Allen as someone the team rides with even on an off day.

injuries.detail: Left the game; Brady said he had no report yet and will evaluate.

signals.claim: Cook will keep getting the ball despite fumbling in consecutive games.
signals.note: Brady publicly backed Cook as the lead runner, so his workload looks safe despite ball-security worries.
signals.quote: that's not going to stop me from giving you the ball the next play

signals.claim: Ty Johnson made a bigger impact on offense, with a fourth-down play and a third-down conversion.
signals.note: Johnson showed explosive playmaking and could carve out a larger change-of-pace or pass-game role.
signals.quote: Ty's on the field. Good things usually happen.

signals.claim: Gore did an outstanding job the first two weeks and was brought back into the mix this game.
signals.note: The comments about Johnson's return and Gore suggest a shared backfield, so Gore's role bears watching.
signals.quote: Frank obviously did an outstanding job the first two weeks

signals.claim: Rousseau will keep rushing from a two-point stance with eyes in the backfield and keep his confidence going.
signals.note: Back-to-back two-sack games and a role tweak make him a rising IDP option.
signals.quote: He's playing a little different position. He has eyes in the backfield.

signals.claim: Kincaid fumbled while fighting for extra yards; Brady wants better ball security but not less effort.
signals.note: A turnover is a mild concern, but Brady framed it as a team-wide coaching issue rather than singling out Kincaid.
signals.quote: I want our guys fighting for extra yards

signals.claim: Benford's injury will be evaluated; no update is available yet.
signals.note: If he misses time, Hairston and Igbinosun step into bigger roles.
signals.quote: Nothing yet.

signals.claim: Igbinosun stepped in after Benford went down and will keep getting opportunities.
signals.note: He is first in line for snaps if Benford is out.
signals.quote: that guy definitely doesn't blink

signals.claim: Hairston was in the mix after Benford went down and wants to bounce back from a rough drive.
signals.note: Hairston may see more snaps if Benford is out, though he had a costly early play.
signals.quote: Max is going to want that first drive back

signals.claim: Gardner-Johnson is back on the field after a week of practice and made a big interception.
signals.note: He is back in the defensive back rotation and is a playmaker for IDP leagues.
signals.quote: So proud of CD man. Just finally getting out there.

signals.claim: Allen had an off day with decisions he wants back, but the team will keep riding with him.
signals.note: No role concern, though pass protection issues could affect his efficiency.
signals.quote: we're always going to ride along with Josh

topics.detail: Brady took the blame for five turnovers and said the team cannot gloss over it just because it won. He promised better play calling and more coaching of detail.
Brady will review the breakdowns that led to hits on Josh Allen and said the review starts with his own play calling.
Brady said the new stadium is loud even in a day game and that he has nothing of note on conditions yet.

title: Dave Canales evaluates Week 3 game vs. Browns
headline: Bryce Young worked through a lower-body issue but finished the game, while Jalen Coker (quad) and Michael Jackson (groin) did not return; the run game and red zone execution need work.
summary: Canales said the game came down to execution, with the Panthers settling for field goals in red-zone and fringe opportunities and missing turnover chances on defense. He cited untimely penalties and a costly roughing-the-passer call on Deshaun Watson's late drive, saying the team must rush with more discipline and keep Watson contained. He credited Browns coach Todd Monken's team for a well-executed plan and said the Panthers matched their energy but not their execution. On the offense, he said the line struggled to handle Cleveland's quick front early, and the run game only settled in late, with the touchdown drive built on runs and play-action. Bryce Young was under pressure and at times worked through a lower-body issue that Canales said may have affected some throws, but he was cleared and finished the game. Canales said Darren Waller's sitting out of some red-zone snaps reflected play-call mixing and tendency balancing, and that Waller's role in the package is something they will review. He praised John Metchie III, Brycen Tremayne and David Moore for stepping up in the passing game, and said the team will review the fourth-and-one decisions and other play calls in detail.

injuries.detail: Lower-body issue; worked through it, cleared to return and finished the game. Full evaluation pending.
Quad injury that lit up during the game; could not return due to pain and strength testing.
Groin injury after chasing across the field; was not putting weight on it and was nowhere close to returning. Extent unknown.
Quad injury on the touchdown play at the end; will be evaluated this week and he would not have returned.

signals.claim: Lower-body injury will get a full evaluation this week; status for next game unknown.
signals.note: Lower-body issue may have affected accuracy and mobility, so his availability and efficiency need monitoring.
signals.quote: He's working through something. But he was able to finish.

signals.claim: Role in the red-zone package is something the staff will look at; he sat out some red-zone snaps.
signals.note: Waller was sitting out key red-zone snaps, which could cut into his touchdown upside if it continues.
signals.quote: Darren has his role in his package as well. That's something we can look at.

signals.claim: Stepped up in the passing game and was coming open late over the middle.
signals.note: Canales praised him for stepping in when other receivers could not go, which supports a bigger role in the passing game.

signals.claim: Led a second-half push and is a reliable option in the passing game.
signals.note: Canales singled him out for the second-half push, pointing to a larger role for a receiver.
signals.quote: I'm glad we have guys like John Metchie.

signals.claim: Stepped up in the passing game during the second half.
signals.note: Named among the players who stepped up in the passing game, which could give him a bigger target share.

topics.detail: Canales said red-zone and fringe opportunities ended in field goals instead of touchdowns and that untimely penalties hurt the team. He wants the team to be smarter in those spots.
Canales said the team must contain Deshaun Watson better and rush with discipline, and admitted the roughing-the-passer decision extended a Browns drive.
The line struggled to handle Cleveland's quickness early, and the run game only settled late. Canales said the team still has not captured an efficient run game this season.
Canales said going for it on fourth and one was an easy decision, though the team missed some execution, including a missed throw to a corner-route option.

title: Zac Taylor Meets With Media Following Week 3 | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Bengals fall 30-27 at Pittsburgh; Kyle Dugger was banged up late with no clear injury update
summary: Taylor said the game got away in the fourth quarter, where all three phases had chances to win and didn't capitalize. He acknowledged Pittsburgh earned the win and said the Bengals now have a chance next week to show what they're made of after a 2-1 start. On the final drive, he thought the offense was moving into field goal range near the 38 and was going for the win rather than settling for a kick, and he said the defense needed to get a stop and get the ball back. He pointed to a big explosive play and a holding call as the key moments on Pittsburgh's last drive. Taylor called the loss disappointing, said the team had chances it didn't take, and said special teams were a big part of the game with a roughing-the-kicker penalty and a muffed punt costing ten points. He said he wouldn't pinpoint why the defense allowed 411 yards and would review the tape before giving a fuller answer the next day. He credited Pittsburgh's quarterback with hitting RPOs and buying time, and said the Steelers have a good coaching staff and players. Asked about injuries, he said both Kyle Dugger and another defensive back were banged up, and he downplayed whether the opponent's quarterback situation affected the game.

injuries.detail: Taylor said he was banged up in the game, with no specific status or designation given.

signals.claim: Was banged up during the game; no official status or practice timeline given.
signals.note: A safety who left and was replaced late creates uncertainty for next week's snap count and availability.
signals.quote: Both of them were banged up.

topics.detail: Taylor said a roughing-the-kicker penalty and a muffed punt cost the team ten points and swung momentum.
The defense allowed 411 yards and failed to get a key stop in the fourth quarter; Taylor will review the tape before explaining what went wrong.
Taylor said the offense was driving to win near the 38 when the fumble happened, and the defense couldn't stop a late explosive drive.
Taylor credited Pittsburgh's offense with effective RPOs and quick throws, and said the Steelers have good coaches and players.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference | Week 3 vs. Carolina Panthers
headline: Browns beat Carolina 21-18 to go 2-1; Deshaun Watson's late scramble and two-point conversion stood out, and Harold Fannin Jr. and Mekhi Blackmon earned praise, but Monken says the offense is well short of its potential.
summary: Monken framed the win around resiliency and the team's togetherness, crediting the defense for playing hard and noting the offense was not coached or played well enough. He said the second half swung on turnovers, a kickoff return giveaway, and a failed fourth-down attempt that left the defense to hold on at the end. Monken praised Deshaun Watson for bouncing back after a hit, saying Watson's late scramble and two-point conversion were a credit to him despite a rough stretch. He said Watson's ability to make plays with his legs is one of his strengths, while his throwing still needs work. On the ground game, Monken said the backs were more downhill and the run game improved, though there is still a lot of work to do. He praised Harold Fannin Jr. as a physical, hard-to-match tight end who is starting to come along, and said Mekhi Blackmon grew more comfortable after replacing Tyson Campbell early in the game. Monken also said Mason Graham is developing into a consistent player and that young players take time to grow. The Browns now face the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday night in a division game that puts them in a first-place tie.

injuries.detail: Went down after a hit and was told to come out; he popped up and insisted he was fine, and he returned to the game and made the late scramble and two-point play. Monken said he did not know right away that Watson would return.

signals.claim: His ability to scramble and run will remain a key part of the offense.
signals.note: His rushing production (three first downs and a touchdown on scrambles in the first half) adds a floor to his fantasy output even when the passing game struggles.
signals.quote: But he's always going to have the ability to make plays with his feet.

signals.claim: Is developing into a bigger part of the passing game, with more targets planned as the offense improves.
signals.note: A strong game against a division opponent with the coach calling him a hard matchup suggests his role is growing.
signals.quote: Harold is really starting to come along, you know, as a player.

signals.claim: Played more snaps and became more comfortable as the game went on after coming in for Tyson Campbell early.
signals.note: Blackmon's increased playing time as a cornerback starter adds to his fantasy-irrelevant but depth-chart-relevant value; the coach expects him to keep growing.
signals.quote: You know like you're going to have your moments.

signals.claim: Is one of the young players expected to grow into more consistent play.
signals.note: Monken's praise suggests Graham is developing into a reliable defensive contributor, though the comments are general rather than a specific role change.
signals.quote: he is one of those and we're going to be less flashy and more consistent

signals.claim: Was targeted late in the game, but the offense's choppy drives limited his opportunities this week.
signals.note: Boston's production depends on the offense getting into a rhythm, which the coach admitted it did not do this week.

topics.detail: Monken said the run game improved, especially before halftime when runs moved the team into the red zone, but he wants the backs to hit it more downhill and more consistently.
Monken defended going for it on fourth-and-one at the end, saying a field goal was about 50-50, and admitted the timeout situation hurt them.
The defense received heavy praise for holding late and for its effort, which Monken called the reason the team won.
Monken said the home crowd made a difference late and that the Browns are now tied for first place in the division with Pittsburgh.

title: Campbell on Week 3 performance
headline: Gibbs looked dominant down the stretch and Goff was praised for a steady game, while Brian Branch was locked in at safety in a 2-1 win over the Jets.
summary: Campbell opened by praising the Jets for playing hard and called the 2-1 win a result of all three phases coming through after last week's Thursday night loss. He credited the defense, and specifically coordinator Kevin Shepherd's call, for the late stop that ended with Chuck Clark forcing a fumble and Jack Campbell recovering it. Campbell said Jahmyr Gibbs found another gear in the second half as the blocking improved, and he noted Gibbs' value on downhill runs and in the passing game. He said offensive coordinator Drew (Campbell didn't name him in full) called a good game that spread the ball around, and he praised Jared Goff's decision-making and patience. On defense, Campbell said Brian Branch was locked in all week, took full-speed padded reps, and played well at safety with three tackles for loss. He said Roger McCreary got a look outside while still being used at nickel, and that Ennis Rakestraw and Rock Ya-Sin were also in the rotation. Campbell also described Isaac TeSlaa's touchdown cutback and said Jets pressure was a factor in the run game.

signals.claim: Gibbs was a key contributor late in the game and will continue to be used heavily in both the run and pass game, with some load management.
signals.note: Gibbs was singled out as the late-game difference-maker, and the coach framed him as a 'use him but keep him fresh' piece, which supports continued heavy involvement.
signals.quote: he hit another gear once we got him going there, particularly in the second half.

signals.claim: Goff is playing at a high level and the offense will keep putting a lot on him at the line of scrimmage.
signals.note: Campbell praised Goff's decision-making, audibles, and quick throws, which supports continued high passing volume.
signals.quote: Just the guy playing at a high level at the quarterback position.

signals.claim: Branch is starting at safety and made a significant impact against the Jets.
signals.note: Branch's three tackles for loss and his confirmed role as a starting safety make him a useful IDP option going forward.
signals.quote: he was locked in all week. He got full speed reps at it, padded work.

signals.claim: Clark's forced fumble was a game-changing play and the defense is valued for his contributions.
signals.note: Clark's game-ending forced fumble is a notable defensive play that could matter for IDP scoring.
signals.quote: you know, Chuck Clark comes up with a huge fumble and then Jack recovering it

signals.claim: McCreary got an outside look but will still play nickel, and the coach described rotating several defensive backs.
signals.note: The defensive back rotation is still fluid, so McCreary's role is uncertain for IDP purposes.
signals.quote: let's give Roger a shot down there outside and still use him though at nickel

topics.detail: The Lions beat the Jets to go 2-1 after a Week 2 Thursday night loss. Campbell said the team showed its identity and won by playing all three phases well.
Campbell said the team deliberately spread snaps among defensive backs, including McCreary, Derrick Moore, and Ennis Rakestraw, and that they can use any of them if needed.
Campbell described a deliberate effort to involve more players, with TeSlaa's deep catch and cutback touchdown highlighted as examples of spreading the ball out.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Texans at Colts, Three Takeaways & Moving Forward
headline: Texans fall to 0-3; Nico Collins is progressing toward a return, and Mario Edwards is being evaluated for a knee injury of unknown extent.
summary: Ryans said Houston is 0-3 and that the loss starts with him, adding that he has not coached well enough and must do better. He felt the week of preparation went well and the players brought the energy he asked for, but game-day execution fell short. He defended the late-half decisions, saying he reviews the clock and timeout situations and weighs options, and that the kickoff was aimed at the goal line but went into the end zone for a touchback. The defense created three takeaways, and the defensive line played well at times, but the unit could not get off the field on third down, and the offense struggled to sustain drives against Indianapolis's third-down conversions. On the fourth-and-one decision, Ryans said he wanted to push forward and trusted the play call, and the late-half Hail Mary call was chosen over a field-goal attempt. He will take 24 hours, review the film, and reset before deciding on changes. He noted the injury to Mario Edwards (knee) is still being evaluated and further testing is coming. He credited several receivers for big plays and said Nico Collins is progressing well and they will see if he can return this week.

injuries.detail: Knee injury; still being evaluated, extent not yet known, further testing planned.
Progressing well; the team will see this week whether he can get back on the field.

signals.claim: Return to action is possible this week, pending progress
signals.note: A return would restore Houston's top receiver; Ryans was non-committal, so monitor the final injury report.
signals.quote: Niko's been progressing really well.

signals.claim: Made a key late-game catch that set up a scoring chance
signals.note: Ryans singled him out for a finishing catch, which suggests a meaningful role in late-game situations.
signals.quote: an outstanding catch by Hutch there to finish

signals.claim: Made a big catch in the game and is part of the rotating pass-catcher group
signals.note: Ryans praised his play, supporting his place in the pass-game rotation.
signals.quote: J. Wayne caught a big one there.

signals.claim: Knee injury extent still unknown; further testing planned
signals.note: Defensive line availability is uncertain until testing is complete.
signals.quote: We're still evaluating Mario for the knee.

topics.detail: Houston is 0-3. Ryans said he will take 24 hours to review and reset, and changes may follow, with the focus on offensive line play and third-down execution.
The defense forced three takeaways but could not get off the field on third down, which allowed Indianapolis to sustain drives.
Ryans defended going for it on fourth-and-one and choosing a Hail Mary over a field-goal attempt late in the half, and said he reviews these decisions himself.
The kickoff was aimed at the goal line but went into the end zone for a touchback; Ryans said kicking to the end zone was not an option in that spot.

title: Shane Steichen: Colts vs. Texans postgame
headline: Colts beat Houston 19-17 with Spencer Shrader's game-winning field goal despite a groin tweak in warmups; Josh Downs and Keenan Allen were the main pass-game targets, and DeForest Buckner is back to form.
summary: Steichen praised the defense for holding Houston to 223 total yards and five three-and-outs, with Buckner and Tuimoloau each recording a sack. He said the team showed resilience to win late. The kicker, Spencer Shrader per the transcript, tweaked his groin about 15 minutes before the game in warmups, was cleared after treatment, and then made a game-winning field goal; Rigo handled kickoffs. Steichen said the team called passes to set up a makeable field goal, with Keenan Allen's slant catch on third down leaving them at fourth-and-one before the kick. On offense, he said Daniel Jones was efficient and protected the ball reasonably well despite three turnovers, and he credited Josh Downs for explosive plays and a strong rapport with Jones. He said Tyler Warren had many underneath catches that lacked yards, and the staff will keep developing that role. He called the win important because it was a division game and the team is now 1-2, and he said the team will travel to London next.

injuries.detail: Tweaked groin in warmups about 15 minutes before the game, was cleared, and kicked the game-winning field goal (not on the listed roster).
Returned from a significant injury and is playing at his usual level; Steichen praised his preparation.

signals.claim: Has fully returned from a significant injury and is playing at his usual level.
signals.note: Confirms his health and ongoing defensive production after a serious injury.
signals.quote: he's the all time pro

signals.claim: Continues to be a featured target with explosive plays, end-breaker shots, and option routes.
signals.note: Consistent explosive-play production and a strong rapport with Daniel Jones keep him a reliable WR option.
signals.quote: He keeps showing up.

signals.claim: Played efficiently despite three turnovers; the staff is focused on ball security in the pocket.
signals.note: A positive efficiency review despite turnovers supports his starting outlook, though ball security is a concern.
signals.quote: he was efficient throwing the football.

signals.claim: Was targeted on deep end breakers and a late third-down slant that set up the field goal.
signals.note: He is a key option in the passing game in critical situations.
signals.quote: hit Keenan on the slant

signals.claim: Got several underneath catches but few yards; the staff will keep developing his role.
signals.note: Volume was there, but yardage was low, so his fantasy value depends on how the role expands.
signals.quote: we'll continue to develop that and keep working it.

topics.detail: Steichen credited communication, tackling, third-down execution, and run defense for holding Houston to 223 total yards and five three-and-outs.
The team called passes to get into field goal range and used Shrader's leg range, though Steichen said the ideal kick spot is around the 35.
Steichen called the win a big division result early in the season, moving the team to 1-2, and said the team will head to London next.

title: Andy Reid: 'We Knew It [Would] Be Four Quarters of Football, And That's What It Took' | Postgame Press Conference - NFL Week 3
headline: No player-specific news from Reid's postgame presser; the Chiefs are 3-0 after a four-quarter win over Miami, with no injuries reported so far.
summary: Reid opened by saying the team has no injuries to report so far, which he seemed a bit surprised to be asked about. He praised Miami's coach and said the Dolphins are a young team that flies around, adding that the Chiefs expected a four-quarter game and that is what it took. He said the team has plenty to work on but was pleased to be 3-0. He highlighted a second-half defensive stand and said the offense took advantage of some of those stops. He called special teams solid. When asked what he liked about Miami's coach and group, Reid said the main point he made to the coach was that his players play hard on every snap, which shows they listen and trust him, and he called the coach sharp with a good staff. Reid named no individual Chiefs players, so there are no fantasy-specific signals from this session.

topics.detail: Chiefs beat the Dolphins in a four-quarter game to move to 3-0. Reid said the team has more to work on, with a few things to fix going forward.
Reid credited a second-half stand by the defense as a key part of the win.
The offense capitalized on some of those defensive stops, per Reid. No specific players or plays were named.
Reid described the special teams performance as solid.
Reid said there were no injuries to report so far, though he didn't name any players.

title: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh Postgame Press Conference vs. Bills
headline: Harbaugh made no personnel or scheme changes after the Bills loss, citing red-zone failures and penalties, and named no players for fantasy purposes.
summary: Harbaugh called the loss painful and said the team did not get it done, even though the defense forced five turnovers and the offense had chances to capitalize. He said the team has not been good enough yet and framed the result as shared, with no individual singled out. He pointed to finishing drives: the offense moved the ball, but it did not score in the end zone, including a drive that reached the 10 and stalled with second-and-goal. When asked about penalties that set back scoring chances, he said they were costly and that the team has not been good enough in critical moments. He said he would review the tape before evaluating individual performances and declined to say who played well or poorly. Asked about significant offensive changes, he said no, and that the staff and players believe in the approach. He said his focus is on the current game and chipping away at problems rather than on the season's expectations.

topics.detail: Harbaugh said the offense moved the ball but failed to finish, including a second-and-goal from the 10-yard line that ended without points. He said the team left points on the field.

Harbaugh acknowledged a costly penalty that moved the offense back at a critical moment, but gave no explanation for the recurring issue beyond saying the team has not been good enough in those spots.

Harbaugh said there are no significant offensive changes planned and did not confirm any disconnect between the scheme, coaching, and execution. He said he cannot say for sure whether the problems are mental lapses or comfort with the offense.
A reporter mentioned injuries, but Harbaugh did not name any players or give a status update.
Harbaugh said nobody is happy with the result and that the team needs to get better and move forward.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 9/27: "We have to fix a lot of things"
headline: Vrabel is openly worried about the Patriots after a Week 3 loss to Jacksonville. Drake Maye's turnovers and hesitation are the focus, Morgan Moses was pulled early for Caleb Lomu, and the run defense got pushed around.
summary: Vrabel opened by saying his concern level for the team is very high, and he repeatedly put the blame on himself. He said the Patriots are not taking care of the football, are not making good decisions, and are being beaten by turnovers, penalties, sudden-change situations and missed red zone chances. On Drake Maye, he insisted the quarterback knows the formations and plays but needs to react to defenses with more confidence. He said Maye shouldn't force things and sometimes wants it too badly, and he stressed that the people around him have to protect him and do their jobs. He described Maye as a young 24-year-old who shouldn't play like a robot, and said he had not seen this kind of turnover problem in practice. He also pointed to pre-snap penalties, saying Jacksonville's pass rushers counted the snap and the team jumped. On the offensive line, he said he took Morgan Moses out early because the game was lost and he wanted to get Caleb Lomu reps, and he wasn't aware of any job in jeopardy. He said the run defense struggled because the team got tired, missed a ton of tackles and couldn't get off the field on third down. He called for fixing things quickly before a road game at Buffalo.

signals.claim: Maye will work to correct his decision-making and ball security, and the coaches expect he can fix the hesitation and turnovers.
signals.note: Maye's turnovers and hesitation are a real concern for his fantasy floor, especially on the road against Buffalo, although Vrabel is publicly backing him.
signals.quote: We haven't made good decisions with the football.

signals.claim: Moses was pulled in garbage time so Caleb Lomu could get reps, and Vrabel isn't aware of his starting job being in jeopardy.
signals.note: A shaky right tackle situation could affect Maye's protection and the offense's efficiency.
signals.quote: let's get Caleb some, some reps.

signals.claim: Lomu got playing time late in the loss when Vrabel pulled Moses.
signals.note: He is a backup to monitor for offensive line changes, but this was framed as a decision made in a lost game rather than a change.

topics.detail: Vrabel said turnovers, missed red zone opportunities, pre-snap penalties and sudden-change breakdowns are what beat the team, and that these are areas where they are usually good.
The defense got tired, missed tackles and let Jacksonville push piles. Vrabel said that if you don't get off the field on third down it creates more chances for opponents.
Vrabel said everything starts with him, and that he will review the tape and plan a practice schedule that prepares the team better.

title: Postgame Press Conference: Coach John Harbaugh on win over Titans
headline: Harbaugh says Jameis Winston will start next week after a win in tough conditions; Jevon Holland's late interception sealed it, and Brian Burns (MRI pending) is the key injury watch.
summary: Harbaugh credited the defense for holding on in the fourth quarter, singling out Jevon Holland's game-winning interception as a play that defines what the league requires. He described the game as a field-position, turnover, and run-game contest in difficult conditions, and said the punt team and defense flipped the field. He was frustrated with the red zone offense, which penalized itself out of scoring position several times, and called that a major point of emphasis. He praised the rookie kicker for making his field goals in the conditions. Harbaugh said Arvell Reese, who had about 14 tackles, earned a game ball, and he lauded the offensive line and Najee Harris's run game against a strong Titans front. On injuries, Pat Ricard suffered a deep nose laceration and Brian Burns will get an MRI that night, with some hope but no certainty. Harbaugh said Winston's performance would not change the QB plan, which he framed as a matter of available options, but he confirmed Winston will start next week. He also acknowledged a wildcat play at the goal line that he called not one of the team's finer moments.

injuries.detail: Injury under evaluation; MRI scheduled for the evening after the game. Harbaugh said there is some hope but nothing is known until the scan.
Suffered a deep nose laceration in the game, reportedly from a hand or facemask contact; no return timeline given.

title: HC Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (9/27) | Week 3
headline: Glenn praised Geno Smith's performance and said Kenyon Sadiq will get more touches, while Garrett Wilson was cleared from a head evaluation and is fine for this game.
summary: Glenn said Garrett Wilson passed a head evaluation and is fine for this game, and that Dylan Parham has a knee issue he would update later, along with two other unnamed players. He felt the defense played well in the first half against a team with many weapons, but allowed momentum in the second half and made execution and call-related mistakes that he takes responsibility for. He said the offense struggled early but rallied after halftime, and he praised Geno Smith as outstanding, especially for getting the ball to the tight ends after a key player went down. He said Kenyon Sadiq is athletic, smart, and can line up at multiple positions, and that the staff will keep getting him the ball. Glenn called the loss tough and said the team is close but must close the gap, especially in the fourth quarter, in red-zone looks, and in two-minute drills. He also said the defense cannot keep giving up so many points, though he did not want to use the opponent's talent as an excuse. Glenn also described a friendly postgame exchange with Dan Campbell, saying the Jets are supposed to be a different team this year.

title: WATCH: McCarthy on the win over the Bengals
headline: Jaylen Warren was the offensive focal point and took a bigger share of the backfield, while Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington were confirmed as primary targets; Rico Dowdle's role appears to have shrunk.
summary: McCarthy said the offense was much better, with third-down execution as the main emphasis, and credited the early checkdowns and Freiermuth's block for getting things going. He called Jaylen Warren huge and the focal point of the game, saying Warren was limited in some practice work but came up big. On the offensive line, McCarthy said the group played with better point-of-attack and communication, and that the offense benefited from being in its third game together. He explained the starting changes at right tackle and right guard: Max Iheanachor, who had a training camp setback, is ready and got his opportunity, and Brock Hoffman has been pushing for a starting spot after playing multiple interior positions. On the backfield, he said Warren's increased touches came from being more selective with Travis Homer and the other backs, letting Warren take as much as he can. He said the tight ends were conscious targets, with Freiermuth and Darnell Washington both considered primary targets, and that ball distribution across the whole perimeter remains a focus. He praised Patrick Queen's 13-tackle, one-for-loss game and said the defense finished the win, and the team now turns to Cleveland.

injuries.detail: Coach said he is ready after a training camp setback and earned his chance to start at right tackle.

signals.claim: Warren will continue to get as much backfield work as he can handle, with fewer rotations to other backs.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald: "We're Going To Go Back To Work And Get Better"
headline: Macdonald blamed the Washington loss on a minus-three turnover margin and situational mistakes, and gave Jadarian Price and AJ Finley vote-of-confidence comments, while Sam Darnold got credit despite two interceptions.
summary: Macdonald said Seattle lost a close game at Washington, a two-point game late, because of a minus-three turnover margin and poor situational football. He credited Washington's plan and said his team needs to take care of the ball, stack plays, and play complementary football. On Sam Darnold, he said the four-touchdown, two-interception day was a microcosm of the game, and he praised the big plays while stressing the turnovers. He admitted the run game never got going, said he wasn't sure the front was good, and said the team shifted emphasis to the passing game as the weather cleared. He acknowledged the pass rush did not generate enough pressure and that the team didn't hit its mark on the quarterback. On red-zone struggles on both sides of the ball, he said the offense and defense were not good enough, especially in sudden-change situations on defense. He defended Jadarian Price after his fumbles, saying he'll be fine and will figure it out, and praised AJ Finley for a strong job on short notice. He closed by saying the response will come from attacking problems and going through, not around.

signals.claim: Darnold's play kept Seattle in the game; coach praised his big plays while stressing turnovers
signals.note: Coach's praise suggests Darnold is not in danger of losing the job despite two interceptions, though the turnovers will be reviewed.
signals.quote: I thought he made some tremendous plays like on time

signals.claim: Price will be fine and will work through his fumble issues; coach said fumbles are not good business
signals.note: Coach backed Price publicly but said turnovers are unacceptable, so his touch share could be at risk if the fumbles continue.
signals.quote: But he's going to be fine. He's going to figure it out.

signals.claim: Finley handled a short-notice role well and the back-end group was organized
signals.note: Finley's praise after filling in on short notice may keep him in a larger role if the absence continues.
signals.quote: I thought he did a great job.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Saleh says Cam Ward is not being benched after an interception, but says Ward must play smarter with the football; the offense's red-zone failures are the main concern.
summary: Saleh said Cam Ward threw an interception when he could have taken a shot or run in the end zone, and that the team had two timeouts and first-and-goal at the 8, so there was no need to force the throw. He called it a learning process for the young players and said he had no consideration of sitting Ward. He said he'd review the tape with Ward and told him to keep his head up. Saleh said the offense played well in the second half but got into the red zone three times and failed to score twice, and that the first half was not good enough. He said the team needs to start faster on offense and that the defense also failed to finish late. On clock management, he took responsibility for a mike linebacker equipment issue that led to a helmet problem and a timeout. He said the officials missed a stopped-forward-progress call on a runner, and he explained a two-minute rule nuance that kept the clock running on a ball carrier who was pushed backward. Saleh also said kicker 'Sly' was a bit off on a 59-yard attempt, and he would take the points there again. He said Jim, a returner, needs to improve after two lost kickoffs, which he called a point of emphasis. He said an injured player is dealing with an ankle issue and will be tested, and that another player came out of the game with something but finished.

injuries.detail: Dealing with an ankle issue; Saleh said they will test him. Name not clear from the captions.

signals.note: Saleh rejected the idea of sitting him, which supports Ward's usage as the starter, though his turnover issues are a risk.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 09/27/26
headline: Quinn gave game balls to Kain Medrano and Marcus Mariota, while Leo Chenal (undergoing testing) and Percy Butler (concussion protocol) are injury concerns to monitor.
summary: Quinn opened by giving updates on Leo Chenal, who was at the hospital undergoing further testing after a serious-sounding injury but had feeling in his extremities, and said Percy Butler is in the concussion protocol. He said the win was meaningful after two losses, especially given the empty takeaway wall outside his office, and credited captains like Terry McLaurin for setting the tone. Quinn praised Kain Medrano for stepping into the role after Chenal's injury and making an interception, and he gave Medrano and Marcus Mariota game balls. He said Mariota's late keeper was the right call and that he trusts him in crunch time, while noting penalties and false starts that need cleanup. Quinn said McLaurin's intensity and blocking stood out, and that Sonny Styles produced an interception, a forced fumble, and a key coverage play. On the receiver room, he said Antonio Williams will want one play back, but the group's spread of targets was a positive. The team flies to London and Quinn will decide on the travel group after a Monday meeting, with Jayden Daniels's rehab status among the questions.
